# DIY Poké Card

> An independent fan-made trading card creation studio. Not affiliated with The Pokémon Company or Nintendo.

The manual editor is free. Users choose original creature illustrations or their own JPEG, PNG, and WebP photos, edit names and abilities, and preview cards in 2D or with simulated 3D tilt and holographic finishes. The studio exports 945 × 1320 PNG images and self-contained interactive HTML keepsakes. Collections and photo drafts are stored locally in the browser, with JSON backup and import.

Optional AI artwork uses credits and works only when AI services are configured. The regular photo editor does not send photos to the server. Explicitly choosing AI photo transformation sends the photo for processing and requires adult permission. Digital holographic effects are not physical foil printing.

## Useful pages
- [Card maker](https://diypokecard.com/): Live studio and original companion templates.
- [Photo cards](https://diypokecard.com/photo-card-maker): Local photo editing, crop controls, and optional AI processing.
- [Holographic cards](https://diypokecard.com/holographic-card-maker): 2D versus 3D, digital finishes, and interactive downloads.
- [Printing](https://diypokecard.com/printable-trading-cards): A4 or Letter layout, 63 × 88 mm cards, calibration and cut guides.
- [Card ideas](https://diypokecard.com/card-ideas): Twelve prompts with editable starting points.
- [Make a game](https://diypokecard.com/make-a-card-game): A local two-card comparison game and home-play rules.
- [Privacy](https://diypokecard.com/privacy.html)
- [Terms](https://diypokecard.com/terms.html)

This file is a convenience summary, not a guarantee of search indexing or AI citation.

- [Pricing](https://diypokecard.com/pricing): Free manual studio; optional one-time AI packs of 15/$4.99, 40/$9.99, and 90/$19.99 USD. No subscription.
